### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface), dispatchFlowAction (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via AutomationContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3d24c991f2d793a1600e7f25fb0d5f577ed2fff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `80b94ca91a3b22ecd1c4c23a3b154281dbe0be20` — the merge of head `b53b0297da66c321f28074e3b9d646cdba0c4301` into base `a3d24c991f2d793a1600e7f25fb0d5f577ed2fff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 80b94ca91a3b22ecd1c4c23a3b154281dbe0be20 && git checkout 80b94ca91a3b22ecd1c4c23a3b154281dbe0be20
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a3d24c991f2d793a1600e7f25fb0d5f577ed2fff b53b0297da66c321f28074e3b9d646cdba0c4301 && git checkout -B drift-repro a3d24c991f2d793a1600e7f25fb0d5f577ed2fff && git merge --no-ff b53b0297da66c321f28074e3b9d646cdba0c4301

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3d24c991f2d793a1600e7f25fb0d5f577ed2fff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a3d24c991f2d793a1600e7f25fb0d5f577ed2fff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0c325aab39dd155412198d98648510eda9354ec7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts (`buildAutomationContext`), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`dispatchFlowAction`), packages/runtime/src/endpoint-executor.ts (the declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint, a third caller of `buildAutomationContext`), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (where `executionContext` is written), packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts (`seedRunGrants`, `deciderSegmentContext`), packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts (`SeededRunContext`, `runPosture`, `resolveRunDataContext`), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/subflow-node.ts (child context), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts and assemble-execution-context.ts (where a request's rung is derived and carried), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts and security-plugin.ts (the first reader keyed on the carried rung), packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts and packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts (the rung's type), docs/adr/0095 D2/D3, and the merged precedent PR #28098. The rest of the diff (the two test files, the changeset, `record-view-auditing.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs: card #28099 (body; triage 6523377748, which grants the cross-domain member; the claim 6523907984; the os-dev report 6525918906), PR #28167 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the head above), and the head's check-runs. Not the dispatch order. Timestamp of this reading: 2026-10-30T15:14Z.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong:

1. **`AutomationContext.posture?: ExecutionContext['posture']`** (`@objectstack/spec/contracts`). One optional member, typed off the kernel schema (`AuthzPostureSchema.optional()` in `execution-context.zod.ts`), so its accept set is exactly the four ladder literals or absent, never a fresh enum. `ExecutionContext` was already a type import in this file; no new import. `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json` lists `AutomationContext (interface)` by name only and `api-surface-signatures.json` has no entry for it, so no generated artifact moves; `Spec property liveness` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on this head. **Right.**
2. **The trigger door forwards the rung.** `buildAutomationContext` (domains/automation.ts:212) copies `ec.posture` only when it is a non-empty string, where `ec` is `context.executionContext`, which only the dispatcher's identity step writes (http-dispatcher.ts:703; left undefined for an anonymous request at :777). A REST body cannot inject it: the function builds `automationContext` from `params`, `callerParamKeys`, `object`, `event`, then the identity facts off `ec`; a flat body key named `posture` is not in the reserved set, so it falls into `params`; a wrapped one never leaves `params`. All three callers of the function take it: the two trigger routes (automation.ts:2361) and the declared `type: 'flow'` endpoint (endpoint-executor.ts:579). **Right**, and pinned by `flow-run-posture.test.ts` (both routes, the body cells, the anonymous cell).
3. **The action door forwards the rung.** `dispatchFlowAction` (action-execution.ts:2083) spreads the same conditional copy. Its `ec` is the resolved envelope at both entrances: REST `/actions` passes `_context.executionContext` (domains/actions.ts:893) and the MCP `run_action` bridge passes the session's `ec` (action-execution.ts:3555). **Right.**
4. **The rung is only ever the caller's own, never the flow author's, never raised.** A request's `ec.posture` is `grants.posture` from `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, derived by `derivePosture` from capability grants (ADR-0095 D3; resolve-authz-context.ts:780; assemble-execution-context.ts:369). Neither door derives, defaults or widens: absent on the request means no key on the context. On the engine side `seedRunGrants` re-resolves only when `permissions` is not an array (`needsGrants`); a context carrying its grants keeps the forwarded rung as forwarded (the integration cell: `MEMBER` forwarded for `usr_admin` stays `MEMBER`). The flow's author never enters any of these paths. **Right.**
5. **A rung that arrives without grants.** A door forwards positions and permission sets only when non-empty, so a rung can arrive alone. Then `needsGrants` is true, the resolver runs, and the new `else delete` (run-resume.ts:228) means the context ends with the resolution's own rung or none, never the forwarded one. **Right**, pinned by the two "without forwarded grants" cells. One arm is not covered: see ④ finding S1.
6. **`runPosture` safe-parses** the carried value against `AuthzPostureSchema`, so a non-ladder string a door forwarded (the door checks only `string`) is dropped at the data context. **Right.**
7. **Where the rung is read.** `resolveRunDataContext` (runtime-identity.ts:411) copies it onto the user arm's `RunDataContext`; the system arm never reads it. The first enforcement reader is the Layer 0 exemption in `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts:191-208`: `isPlatformAdmin = superuserBypass && platformPosture`, where `platformPosture` is the carried rung when present. The rung alone grants nothing; the superuser bit from the carried permission sets must hold too. **Right**, and it is what makes the member fail closed by construction.
8. **Child and resumed contexts.** `subflow-node.ts:105` spreads the parent's context into the child, so the rung rides beside the grants it came with, as `SeededRunContext`'s docblock says. A suspended run persists its context; a non-decision resume continues under the trigger user's whole identity (ruling A on `FlowSchema.runAs`), rung included, beside that same user's grants. The decision switch `deciderSegmentContext` (run-resume.ts:330) deletes the submitter's rung with their positions, permission sets, peers and email before seeding the decider's. **Right.**
9. **Docs.** `record-view-auditing.mdx` now states a door-started run carries its caller's posture and is served the deployment-level rows the same way; true on this tree. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28099-door-runs-carry-posture-rung.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`; all three are moved by the diff and only those three. `Check Changeset` green.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on both carriers (PR body and changeset body). Read with the fleet's one reader, `readClause2Line` in `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`: both bodies parse `declared / yes / widening`. The arm is right: one optional member added to an exported contract interface; no existing member changes type or meaning; a producer that never sets it and a consumer that ignores it behave as on `main`.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` on both carriers; `readMetadataProtocolLine` parses `declared / none` on both. Right: nothing a metadata author writes changes (no flow key, no accepted value, no default).
- Per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The level matches what the diff publishes.
- Triage 6523377748 granted the cross-domain member and asked for exactly this declaration and this review; the claim's file surface is held (no other `packages/spec` file, no governed path; the `.mdx` sentence was added to the surface by the seat at claim time).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` in the dev report: none to answer.
- Dev observation 1, `SeededRunContext.posture` restating the inherited member. Checked: `SeededRunContext.posture?: AuthzPosture` (`z.input` of the enum) and `AutomationContext.posture?: ExecutionContext['posture']` (`z.infer` of the same enum, optional) are the same literal union; the restatement is type-identical and its docblock stays accurate on this tree. Answered: no action owed in this PR; a later touch of `runtime-identity.ts` may drop it.
- Dev observation 2, `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx:2518` (the trigger route's Identity paragraph: "user, positions, permissions, tenant"). Incomplete, not false; it already omitted `locale` and `email`. The docs-drift check on this PR (comment 6525918010) names `flows.mdx` and `ui/actions.mdx` as pages that name `AutomationContext` / `dispatchFlowAction`. Escalated as **S2 (should-fix)** below: a one-clause docs follow-up, not a reason to hold this PR.
- Check-runs on this head at the time of this record: green `Lint & Repo Gates` and all `Lint ·` legs, `Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test Core (2/8, 7/8, 8/8)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`. **Still pending:** `Test Core (1/8, 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 6/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`. No check-run on this head has concluded red. Those conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not stand in for them, and the PR lands only once every required context is `success`.
- Nothing in the diff touches a governed surface (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green); the PR is a draft with no assignee or reviewer request, per the dispatch's shape.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, the one `hits` file, judged against the triage ruling (forward the caller's own rung beside their positions and permission sets; never derived from the flow's author, never raised) and its first consumers.

The member holds. It is typed off the kernel's resolved rung rather than a new vocabulary; its docblock names the two setters, the as-is rule, the absent-narrows rule, the re-resolution rule, and the system arm, and every one of those sentences is true of the cited code at this head (①.2-①.8). Its first consumer chain, `runPosture` to `resolveRunDataContext` to the Layer 0 exemption, requires the superuser bit from the carried permission sets in addition to the rung, so the member can narrow and never widen on its own.

Attempts to break it:

- **A missing rung that defaults upward.** Both doors add no key; `runPosture` answers `undefined`; the Layer 0 gate then falls back to the capability probe, which is a strict subset of the rung's derivation (ADR-0099 I3) and so can only narrow. The integration suite's CONTROL cell measures the pre-fix shape (grants, no rung) served the organization row only. Holds.
- **A persisted context carrying one segment's rung into a later resume under a different caller.** A non-decision resume (screen, wait, SLA, engine continuation) keeps the trigger user's `userId`, grants and rung together, by ruling A; the rung never stands under another person's id. A decision resume deletes it before the decider is seeded. Holds.
- **An approval segment's run.** `deciderSegmentContext` deletes `positions`, `permissions`, `org_user_ids`, `posture`, `email`, then `seedRunGrants(..., 'deciding')` with `needsGrants` true, so the segment carries the decider's own rung or none; a `runAs: 'system'` run returns before seeding and its data arm never reads the rung. The new `else delete` is a no-op there (already deleted) and the right thing on the trigger path. Holds.
- **An agent principal on behalf of a platform administrator with a narrowed ceiling.** The request's `ec.posture` is the envelope's own (assemble-execution-context.ts:369); the door forwards it beside the narrowed permission sets; run setup keeps both as carried. The run reads what the same agent request reads, and the Layer 0 gate still asks the superuser bit of the narrowed sets. Holds.
- **Body injection.** Refused by construction and pinned (①.2).

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix, not blocking).** `seedRunGrants`'s fail-safe arm (run-resume.ts, the `catch`): when the resolver throws on a context that needed grants, the run keeps the user's unresolved identity (baseline member fallback) and, since this PR, also keeps a rung a door forwarded without grants. Before this PR no rung could exist on a context whose grants were never resolved. The first reader still refuses the deployment-level rows (no superuser bit, so `isPlatformAdmin` is false), and the rung is still the caller's own, never raised, so this is not a widening; but the docblock's sentence "a rung stands only beside the grants it was derived from" is not held in that arm, and the warning's "falls back to baseline member permissions (not elevated)" is then written over a context that still carries `PLATFORM_ADMIN`. Fix: in the `catch`, when `needsGrants`, `delete (runContext as SeededRunContext).posture` as the success arm does, and pin it with one cell (resolver rejects, forwarded rung alone, data context carries no `posture`). May land here or as a one-hunk follow-up on `run-resume.ts`.
- **S2 (should-fix, not blocking).** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx:2518`, the trigger route's Identity paragraph, lists the forwarded identity as "user, positions, permissions, tenant"; add the posture rung (and, while there, locale and email, which the same doors already forward). Docs-only; `ui/actions.mdx` to be re-read for the same sentence per the drift check.

No must-fix.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b53b0297da66c321f28074e3b9d646cdba0c4301`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts (`seedRunGrants`, `deciderSegmentContext`), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`setUserGrantsResolver`), packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts (`buildAutomationContext`) and packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`dispatchFlowAction`) re-read for the facts the doors forward, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx (the trigger route's Identity paragraph), and everything the superseded record 6526196044 read on 0c325aab. The rest of the diff (the two test files, the changeset, `record-view-auditing.mdx`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

This record is a DELTA review: it supersedes record 6526196044 (PASS on `0c325aab39dd155412198d98648510eda9354ec7`) and names the new head, which is that head plus one commit, `b53b0297`, taking both should-fixes of that record. The delta touches five files: `run-resume.ts` (one hunk moved), `runas-user-posture-rung.integration.test.ts` (one new cell), `automation-service.ts` (docblock only), `flows.mdx` (one paragraph) and the changeset (one bullet reworded, one added). Nothing else moved between the two heads; judgments ① to ④ of 6526196044 stand where this record does not restate them. Inputs: card #28099 (body; triage 6523377748; the claim 6523907984, amended to add `flows.mdx` to the surface; the dev report 6525918906), PR #28167 (body, unchanged since 6526196044; file list, now nine paths; the net diff against `main` at the head above; the delta diff `0c325aab..b53b0297`), the delta claim 6526622532, and the head's check-runs. Timestamp of this reading: 2026-10-30T15:35Z.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **S1 taken, and taken the stricter way.** `seedRunGrants` (run-resume.ts:205-210) now runs `if (needsGrants) delete posture` before the resolver guard, where `needsGrants` is "`permissions` is not an array". The success arm is byte-identical to `main`'s (#28098's line: `if (grants.posture) posture = grants.posture`), and the `else delete` from 0c325aab is gone. So a rung stands on a run context after setup only if (a) the context arrived with its permission sets, in which case it is kept as forwarded (the carried-grants invariant of #28098 is untouched), or (b) the resolver answered grants carrying one. A resolver that throws, answers `undefined`, answers grants with no rung, or is not wired (`this.userGrantsResolver` falsy; `setUserGrantsResolver` accepts `null`, engine.ts:4118) leaves none. **Right**: this closes the arm 6526196044 S1 named (the `catch`) and the unwired arm it did not name.
2. **Side effects of the up-front delete.** It fires on a `runAs: 'system'` context with no permission sets too; harmless, the system arm of `resolveRunDataContext` never reads the rung, and the member's docblock already says the rung is absent on such a run's data context. The decision switch (`deciderSegmentContext`) had already deleted `posture` with the submitter's other facts before calling `seedRunGrants(..., 'deciding')`, so the new line is a no-op there. An agent principal's narrowed ceiling, a door envelope with grants, a subflow/map child and a resumed segment all carry `permissions`, so none is touched. A record-change run arrives with no rung, so nothing to delete. **Right.**
3. **The new test cell** (integration test, envelope layer) runs a rung-alone context against three resolvers in turn: one that rejects, one answering `undefined`, and `null` (unwired), and asserts the recording node's data context has `isSystem: false`, the member's `userId` and no `posture` key. It covers all three arms of ①.1's "leaves none". **Right.** It runs in the `Test Core` shards, which have not reported on this head yet (③).
4. **S2 taken, with a correction to the superseded record.** The Identity paragraph (flows.mdx:2518-2525) now says the caller's identity (user, positions, permissions, tenant, posture rung) and language are forwarded as the caller's request resolved them; that the rung is the caller's own, never the flow author's, never raised, and that a request without one starts a run without one; and that run setup adds the user's email and organization peers. Re-read against both doors at this head: `buildAutomationContext` forwards `userId`, `positions`, `permissions` (non-empty only), `tenantId`, `posture`, `locale`; `dispatchFlowAction` the same set. Neither forwards `email`; `seedRunGrants` seeds `email` and `org_user_ids` from the resolver (`needsEmail`, `needsPeers`). So the paragraph is true on this tree, and record 6526196044's S2 was wrong to say the doors already forward email: the dev's correction stands. **Right.**
5. **The `hits` file.** The docblock of `AutomationContext.posture` now reads: when run setup resolves the grants itself it drops any forwarded rung and takes the rung off that same resolution; grants that stay unresolved (the resolver rejects, answers nothing, or is not wired) leave the run with none; so a rung stands only beside the grants it was derived from. Every clause is true of run-resume.ts at this head (①.1). No type, name or member changed; `api-surface/contracts.json` still lists the interface by name only. **Right.**
6. **Changeset.** The "Only beside the grants it came from" bullet now matches ①.1 exactly, and a "Docs" bullet names the `flows.mdx` paragraph and the `record-view-auditing.mdx` sentence. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from 6526196044 and re-read on this head: `patch` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, the three packages the diff moves; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` parse `declared` on both carriers through `readClause2Line` / `readMetadataProtocolLine` in `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (changeset at `b53b0297`, PR body as it stands). A non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). The delta adds no member, no key and no accepted value. Matches.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The two should-fixes of 6526196044 are both taken (①.1, ①.4); no new dev flag and no `open_questions` entry on the delta.
- Dev observation 1 from the previous round (`SeededRunContext.posture` restating the inherited member) is unchanged and still no action owed.
- The claim surface was amended before the `flows.mdx` edit (comment 6523907984 names "the trigger route's Identity paragraph only"); the delta's hunk is that paragraph and nothing else on the page. Surface held.
- PR body: unchanged since the previous record.
